title: Working with Family Offices to Deepen Investments in Local Companies
what_it_is: Working with Family Offices to Deepen Investments in Local Companies

sections.label: Family office local investment rules
sections.summary: Since April, single family offices applying for tax incentives must allocate at least 10% or S$10 million, whichever is lower, to local investments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: First, single family offices (SFOs) applying for tax incentive schemes have been required since April this year to allocate at least 10% or S$10million of their assets, whichever is lower, to local investments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Local investments may include: one, equities listed on Singapore exchanges; two, private equity investments in unlisted Singapore-incorporated companies; or three, qualifying debt securities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Second, MAS and Enterprise Singapore have set up a number of platforms to connect local companies to potential investors, including family offices.

sections.label: Global-Asia Family Office Circle
sections.summary: MAS and EDB support the Wealth Management Institute's Global-Asia Family Office Circle, which encourages family offices to co-invest and develop philanthropy and sustainable investment strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Third, MAS and EDB have supported the Wealth Management Institute’s Global-Asia Family Office Circle, which aims to encourage family offices here to make co-investments in companies as well as develop strategies in areas such as philanthropy and sustainable investments.

sections.label: Family Office Development Team
sections.summary: MAS and EDB set up the Family Office Development Team in 2019 to coordinate Government efforts, widen asset vehicles and launch skill maps for family office advisers and professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Member may know that in 2019, MAS and EDB jointly set up the Family Office Development Team or FODT to coordinate a whole-of-Government effort to ensure Singapore remains a really relevant and attractive location for family offices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The first focus area is to enhance and widen the operating environment to broaden the suite of asset vehicles, such as variable capital companies (VCCs), that are available to these family offices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For example, MAS and the Institute of Banking and Finance launched these skill maps for family office advisers, including those at banks and tax or legal firms; and also, for entry level professionals employed in family offices; and also, then, management level executives who head and also run these offices.

sections.label: MAS training fee co-funding
sections.summary: MAS has co-funding schemes to offset training fees for professionals attending courses accredited against the skill maps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS has available co-funding schemes in place to offset the training fees for professionals attending these courses that have been accredited against these skill maps.
